evals.name: classification-evidence-and-collisions
evals.prompt: Dry run only: classify four sanitized observations for GET /x/web-interface/view. Existing not-found has codes [-404], http [200], and 200.code-404.not-found.json; its body says the video is missing. Frame A is a complete legacy-format HTTP 404 capture, no business code, same missing-video meaning, captured 2026-09-28T01:00:00Z, no bodyMeta. Frame B is another HTTP 200/code -404 capture with different request query and body than the existing file, no bodyMeta. Frame C is HTTP 200/code 0 with response.body as JSON text and response.bodyMeta {representation: text, source: text, mimeType: application/json}; current example schema rejects bodyMeta. Frame D is HTTP 200/code 78123 with an unexplained opaque message. Give per-frame decisions, exact filenames where applicable, proposed mutations and unresolved items; do not execute CLI commands or edit repository data.
evals.expected_output: Merge A into not-found using its HTTP-only filename; preserve B as a collision; retain C with a compatibility blocker; leave D unclassified with evidence gaps. No invented slug, suffix, discarded metadata or full-success claim.
assertions: Merges frame A into not-found with 404.http-only.not-found.json, retains code -404 and adds HTTP 404.
Preserves the existing recording for B and reports the filename collision without inventing a suffix or variant.
Blocks C on bodyMeta incompatibility while preserving the text body and metadata; does not propose stripping or hiding metadata.
Leaves D unclassified without inventing a semantic glossary entry from code 78123.
Reports unresolved frames and pending validation without claiming a completed import.

evals.name: pipeline-recovery-on-windows
evals.prompt: Dry run only: give an executable recovery plan for importing sources/capture one.har and sources/capture two.har on Windows PowerShell. The CLI has not been built or linked. The working tree has unrelated edits. A previous extract stopped because .raw/GET.x.web-interface.view.yaml was modified; no valid manifest owns that file. Only local results were requested. Assume classification later reports one unsupported bodyMeta frame while other frames can be imported. State commands, working directories, handoffs, failure handling and completion criteria. Include how to check rendering stability when generated files are untracked. Do not run the pipeline or edit repository data.
evals.expected_output: Build and invoke the local CLI, supply explicit quoted HAR paths as one batch, choose fresh --out and pass it to classify, preserve unrelated work, report partial import, compare paths and hashes across two renders, keep delivery local.
assertions: Builds and invokes the local CLI from workflow/cli, passing both spaced HAR paths as one batch.
Uses a fresh --out directory and passes that directory to classify, preserving the modified draft and manifest.
Preserves unrelated changes and keeps delivery local without creating a PR.
Compares generated file paths and content hashes across consecutive renders, including untracked files.
Reports partial completion for the blocked bodyMeta frame even if remaining corpus gates pass.

evals.name: drift-adjudication-and-notes
evals.prompt: Dry run only: assess a drift report, then draft short Chinese endpoint notes; do not apply any canonical edits. The report labels HTTP 404/code -404 as breaking for video.view-info. Existing not-found has HTTP 200/code -404; complete sanitized examples establish identical missing-video meaning in both shells. Another change is a field absent in one sample (BodyNode has no required contract). A third reports data.id changing number to string, but the underlying capture is unavailable. The CLI exited 0. For notes, definition auth is optional, query aid default is 114514 (an observed value), risk-control has schema null and HTTP 412, and request cookies include {{SESSDATA}}. Give one decision per change, version implications, then the proposed notes.md text without inventing live behavior.
evals.expected_output: Reclassify the shell addition as non-breaking; treat single-sample absence as advisory; defer unsupported type-change judgment; do not bump versions in analysis mode or infer no drift from exit 0. Notes distinguish observed defaults, optional auth, untrusted body and masked credentials.
assertions: Reclassifies the confirmed same-meaning shell addition as non-breaking, retaining the existing semantic variant.
Treats one missing field as advisory without deleting the existing schema field.
Defers the unsubstantiated type-change judgment, keeps analysis read-only, and does not treat CLI exit 0 as absence of drift.
Explains that aid default is observed and auth is optional without inventing login or retry guarantees.
Explains schema null as untrusted/unavailable shape and the cookie placeholder as masked, not a usable credential.
